intro: The fourth part of section 34.4 surveys the other psychodynamic and personality schools, about 40 theorists from Karl Abraham to Donald Winnicott, in the chapter's alphabetical order. Some built on Freud, some broke with him, and some came from learning theory, existential philosophy or the measurement of personality. Each entry gives the theorist's years, school, key terms and what the chapter says about psychopathology and treatment, with a comparison table for each group and a shared case, Mr. A, at the end.
objectives: Name each theorist's school or movement and match the key terms to the right person (for example individual psychology to Adler, transactional analysis to Berne, analytic psychology to Jung, self-psychology to Kohut).
Contrast the object relations theorists (Klein, Fairbairn, Balint, Winnicott, Jacobson, Kernberg) on drives, early objects and maternal failure.
Describe the treatment ideas the chapter credits to the schools, such as the corrective emotional experience, logotherapy, will therapy, client-centered therapy and the participant-observer.
Recognize the humanistic and existential thinkers (Allport, Goldstein, Maslow, Rogers, Frankl, Sartre) and what each meant by the self, meaning or freedom.
Tell apart similar names and terms, such as Murray and Murphy, Meyer and Menninger, Anna Freud and Sigmund Freud, and Klein's and Bion's versions of projective identification.
Use the update boxes for later facts: corrected dates for Rado and the Hampstead clinic, and the trials of Kernberg's transference-focused psychotherapy.
